audience: an adult English learner who wants confident, natural restaurant English
domain: realistic conversations among diners, hosts, servers, bartenders, and restaurant managers

collection.title: Restaurant Conversations
collection.description: Handle reservations, menus, dietary needs, ordering, service problems, payment, and takeout with natural, tactful English.

methodology: Teach complete conversational moves rather than isolated menu vocabulary.
Balance courteous directness with the tact expected in present-day American restaurants.
Include both guest-facing and staff-facing language so learners can understand likely replies as well as make requests.
Prefer specific clarification, confirmation, and repair language over vague or overly apologetic wording.
Use pragmatic B2–C1 complexity: managing expectations, negotiating alternatives, resolving errors, and handling social nuance.
Cover quick-service, casual, and full-service dining without tying the material to a particular brand or cuisine.
Keep lines useful on their own while making the likely situation and speaker intention easy to infer.
Reflect common American practices around reservations, substitutions, tipping, splitting checks, leftovers, and takeout.
requirements: Distribute lines across diners, hosts, servers, bartenders, managers, and members of a dining party; do not make every line a customer request.
Avoid repetitive openings such as 'Could you,' 'Can I,' and 'I'd like'; use varied natural sentence shapes.
Include tactful but firm language for allergy safety, incorrect orders, delays, charges, and unacceptable food.
Do not invent restaurant names, app names, loyalty programs, or culture-specific dishes merely to add variety.
Do not turn sentences into vocabulary definitions or etiquette lessons.

sections.title: Reservations & arrival
sections.description: Book, change, confirm, and locate a reservation, then handle waits and walk-in availability.
sections.guidance: Cover phone reservations, online-booking confusion, changing party size or time, late arrivals, walk-ins, wait estimates, holding a table, and host responses.

sections.title: Seating & comfort
sections.description: Negotiate table location, accessibility, space, temperature, noise, and other seating needs.
sections.guidance: Cover booths versus tables, outdoor seating, high chairs, wheelchair access, bags and coats, drafts, sunlight, noise, moving tables, and tactful limits from staff.

sections.title: Understanding the menu
sections.description: Clarify unfamiliar items, ingredients, portions, preparation, availability, and pricing.
sections.guidance: Include descriptions, portion comparisons, cooking methods, market-price questions, sold-out items, specials, side choices, tasting menus, and what is included.

sections.title: Dietary needs & allergies
sections.description: Communicate allergies and dietary restrictions precisely and verify that an order can be handled safely.
sections.guidance: Cover severe allergies, cross-contact, hidden ingredients, vegetarian and vegan needs, gluten and dairy concerns, substitutions, kitchen verification, and declining unsafe accommodation.

sections.title: Recommendations & pairings
sections.description: Ask for and give useful recommendations based on taste, appetite, budget, and drink pairings.
sections.guidance: Include flavor preferences, spice, richness, sharing, value, signature dishes, wine or nonalcoholic pairings, server follow-up questions, and honest comparisons.

sections.title: Ordering & customizing
sections.description: Place a complete order, specify preparation, request reasonable changes, and confirm details.
sections.guidance: Cover doneness, dressings and sauces, sides, add-ons, omissions, courses, shared plates, drinks, substitutions, order read-backs, and limits on modifications.

sections.title: Service & pacing
sections.description: Manage timing, refills, missing items, check-ins, and the pace of a meal without sounding abrupt.
sections.guidance: Include waiting for another guest, spacing courses, needing time, signaling readiness, refills, utensils, clearing plates, time constraints, server updates, and kitchen delays.

sections.title: Problems & resolution
sections.description: Raise concerns about food or service and negotiate a proportionate, professional resolution.
sections.guidance: Cover wrong or missing dishes, unsafe ingredients, temperature and doneness, excessive waits, spilled items, poor service, remake versus removal, manager responses, and fair remedies.

sections.title: Group meals & occasions
sections.description: Coordinate a group order, celebrations, shared food, separate needs, and social decisions at the table.
sections.guidance: Include ordering for a group, sharing etiquette, choosing dishes, late guests, birthdays, business meals, children, alcohol decisions, invitations, and discreet arrangements with staff.

sections.title: Dessert, payment & takeout
sections.description: Finish the meal, resolve the check, tip, package leftovers, and manage pickup or delivery issues.
sections.guidance: Cover dessert and coffee, asking for the check, splitting or combining payment, disputed charges, cards and cash, receipts, tips, boxes, takeout pickup, missing items, and reheating guidance.
